regulations_meta.title: Food Safety and Standards (Packaging) Regulations, 2018
regulations_meta.authority: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)
regulations_meta.enabling_act: Section 92 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (Act No. 34 of 2006)
regulations_meta.scope: All food business operators (FBOs) manufacturing, importing, packing, storing, distributing or selling food articles in India

general_requirements.title: Safety & Inertness of Packaging Materials
general_requirements.summary: Every food business operator shall ensure that the packaging material is in accordance with these regulations and is completely food-grade, safe, and clean.
key_points: Packaging materials must not transfer their constituents to food in quantities injurious to human health.
Must not deteriorate organoleptic (taste, smell, texture, appearance) properties of food.
Must be stored in a clean and hygienic environment prior to use.
Printing inks and adhesives must not come into direct contact with food articles unless specifically certified as safe food-grade inks.

general_requirements.title: Prohibition of Newspaper and Printed Paper for Food Contact
general_requirements.summary: Newspapers, recycled papers, or printed paper materials SHALL NOT be used for storing, wrapping, lining, serving, or absorbing excess oil from cooked or fresh food products.
scientific_reasons: Newspaper printing inks contain dangerous chemical binders, mineral oil saturated hydrocarbons (MOSH), mineral oil aromatic hydrocarbons (MOAH), naphthylamines, and phthalates.
Printing pigments contain heavy metal residues including lead, cadmium, and cobalt.
Hot and oily foods rapidly leach oil-soluble ink solvents directly into the food matrix within seconds of contact.
Printing presses and secondary handling expose newspaper surfaces to pathogenic microorganisms, fecal bacteria, and atmospheric dust.
approved_alternatives: Food-grade greaseproof paper conforming to IS 6615
Food-grade butter paper or baking parchment paper
Virgin cellulose food-grade paper napkins conforming to IS 1060
Traditional clean banana leaves or plant-based leaf wraps

general_requirements.title: Prohibition of Recycled Plastics in Primary Food Packaging
general_requirements.summary: Recycled plastics SHALL NOT be used in packaging material for food articles unless processed through approved decontamination technologies meeting FSSAI circular guidelines.
key_points: Post-consumer untreated plastic recyclates contain chemical impurities, pesticide residues, and plasticizer degradation products.
Only specifically certified food-grade rPET processes compliant with FSSAI direction F.No. RCD-02001/4/2021 are permitted for secondary/tertiary or approved food bottles.

plastics.overall_migration_limit: 60 mg/kg or 10 mg/dm² into food simulants (IS 9845:2020 testing)
plastics.pigments_and_colorants: Must comply with IS 9833 (List of pigments and colorants for use in plastics in contact with foodstuffs)

mandatory_bis_standards.material: Glass containers for food and beverages
Testing for alkali extraction from glass

glass.requirements: Must be inert, neutral, chemically resistant, free from cracks, thermal shock resistant, and contain no lead or toxic heavy metal fluxes.

mandatory_bis_standards.material: Wrought aluminum and aluminum alloys for food packaging
Round tinplate cans for food preservation

metal_and_tinplate.requirements: Must be coated with approved food-grade epoxy, organosol, or polyester lacquers to prevent acidic corrosion and metal leaching (iron, tin, aluminum).

labelling_and_traceability.regulation: Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Regulations, 2020
mandatory_declarations: FSSAI License / Registration logo and 14-digit license number
Name and address of Food Business Operator (Manufacturer/Packer/Marketer)
Veg / Non-Veg symbol (Green dot inside green square / Brown triangle in brown square)
Net quantity, Batch / Lot identification code
Date of manufacture and Use-by / Expiry date
Nutritional information per 100g/100ml and per serve
